title: OpenAPI and Swagger UI
summary: Describe an API, generate its documentation and inspect it in Swagger UI.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: How to Integrate Swagger in Spring Boot | Step-by-Step Tutorial

richText: Describe the API
OpenAPI is a machine-readable description of an HTTP API.
It lists paths, HTTP methods, inputs, responses and authentication requirements.
A schema describes a data structure, including its fields and types.
Swagger UI displays an OpenAPI description in a browser and can send requests to the API.
Generate the description with springdoc
springdoc-openapi generates a description from Spring controllers, data types and annotations.
For a Spring MVC application with Swagger UI, use springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui.
Choose a springdoc release compatible with the project’s Spring Boot version. Boot 3 uses springdoc 2.x; Boot 4 uses springdoc 3.x.
Check the compatibility matrix for the exact Boot release. Older Boot 2 examples use a different springdoc dependency line.
Open the generated documentation
The default OpenAPI JSON path is /v3/api-docs.
The default Swagger UI entry path is /swagger-ui.html. It can redirect to the UI resources.
Add the application’s context path if one is configured.
Security rules can restrict these paths. Allow access only to the documentation routes you intend to expose.

example.title: Enable API documentation in application.properties
description: Use this configuration in an application with a compatible springdoc UI starter.
explanation: api-docs.enabled controls the generated API description endpoint.
These properties enable documentation. They do not make protected endpoints public.

richText: Keep the description accurate
Check the described request fields, response fields and statuses against each controller.
Document failure responses as well as successful responses.
Use DTOs to describe the fields clients can send or receive.
An OpenAPI security scheme describes how a client supplies credentials. Spring Security enforces access separately.
Update the controller annotations or data types that generate the description. Manual changes to generated JSON disappear when it is generated again.
Sending a request from Swagger UI exercises that request. It does not prove that every documented behavior works.
